From: Maya Collins <maya@aerynlabs.com>

Cc: Samir Reddy <samir.reddy@aerynlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Apr 2028 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Optimize toolkit — quant/batching concessions for pilot

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — the latency improvements on our chat flows looked promising. Samir and I pulled together a short RFI to understand the commercial levers we can use to keep pilot costs within our budget while we validate quality. Two quick asks: 

1) We're most concerned about token spend on long-context summarization flows. Can you summarize how batching window and prefix/KV caching reduce billable tokens vs. model quantization?
2) On discounts: what flexibility do you have for a three-month pilot (expected 350M tokens/month) if we agree to a product-integration case study?

I've attached the RFI (Aeryn_RFI.xlsx) with usage scenarios and a baseline cost target. Ideally we'd like a written concession sketch before we jump on a call next week.

Thanks —
Maya Collins
Head of Platform Integrations, Aeryn Labs
[attachment: Aeryn_RFI.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Collins <maya@aerynlabs.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit — quant/batching concessions for pilot

Maya —

Appreciate the RFI and the clear target. High-level answers up front, then a short concession sketch attached.

Short answers:
- Batching window + prefix/KV caching: both reduce total compute and thus billable tokens by reducing redundant compute across requests. For your summarization flows (long context, repeated prefixes), we typically see 30–55% token-equivalent savings depending on cache hit rate and request fan-out. Batching further smooths per-token latency cost — helpful for bursts.
- Quantization: moves CPU/GPU unit cost down (fewer FLOPs or smaller kernels). For most families we onboard (Q4_8 and Q8_0 profiles), you can expect 20–35% unit-cost reduction with minimal quality delta on summarization. There is an interplay: aggressive quantization plus caching yields the best cost per effective token, but we recommend phased QA on your dev prompts.

Attached is a simple concession matrix: proposed pilot rebate (10% on token invoice for month 1, 8% for month 2, 5% month 3) + 100k free inference credits to cover initial tuning runs. We also propose a technical gating clause: we run a short calibration job on your top-20 prompts; if model quality drop >2.5% on our eval set we pause deeper quantization until resolved (we'll share metrics).

Next steps: can we do 45m on Tue 2028-05-02 to walk the matrix and confirm the integration case-study scope? Vanessa + Camila will join to capture operational/terms details.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference runtime
[attachment: proposed_concession_matrix_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: concession posture & margin checks (Aeryn)

Nikhil / Camila —

Quick internal thread before we call Maya/Samir:

1) Concession levels are slightly above our standard pilot baseline. We should tighten the free credit (drop to 75k) unless Aeryn commits to the case study deliverables with publication rights and a 6-month post-pilot buyer-intro clause.
2) The calibration gating is good but operationally heavy; propose we shift language to "automated rollback" — if our eval detects >2.5% QA delta on the canonical prompt set, Redwood will automatically fall back to a non-quant variant while engineering triages. That minimizes product impact for Aeryn.
3) On telemetry: ask Legal if we can retain anonymized eval traces for 90 days for quality regressions — helps us tune quant profiles.

I'll prep a redline to the concession PDF and an alternate credit schedule. Camila, can you confirm SRE runbook for rollback automation and whether it adds any lead time to onboarding?

- Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Regards,
